atoms.text: This guide configures the bucket policy for a video transcoding pipeline that reads source files from the uploads/ prefix of the bucket studio-media-prod and writes MP4 renditions to the renditions/ prefix. The transcoding jobs run under an IAM role named ReelPressJobRole in account 111122223333. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow and Principal set to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ReelPressJobRole"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-prod/uploads/* so the role can read the source files. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-prod/renditions/* so the role can write the output files. Do not include s3:DeleteObject, because the pipeline never removes source files. The role must also hold matching permissions in its own identity policy, since an IAM principal in the same account is evaluated against both policies. After saving the policy, submit a test job and confirm that a rendition object appears under renditions/ with the expected size and duration.

This guide configures the bucket policy for a video transcoding pipeline that reads source files from the uploads/ prefix of the bucket studio-media-prod and writes MP4 renditions to the renditions/ prefix. The transcoding jobs are run directly by the ReelPress service in account 111122223333. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow and Principal set to {"Service": "reelpress.amazonaws.com"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-prod/uploads/* so the service can read the source files. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-prod/renditions/* so the service can write the output files. Do not include s3:DeleteObject, because the pipeline never removes source files. Add a Condition block with StringEquals on aws:SourceAccount set to 111122223333 and ArnLike on aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:reelpress:*:111122223333:job/*, so that jobs from other accounts cannot use the grant. After saving the policy, submit a test job and confirm that a rendition object appears under renditions/ with the expected size and duration.

This guide covers the bucket policy for an OCR pipeline that reads scanned PDF files from the scans/incoming/ prefix of the bucket records-archive-eu and writes searchable text layers to the scans/text/ prefix. The extraction workers run under an IAM user named ocr-batch-user in account 444455556666. Create a statement with Effect set to Allow and Principal set to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:user/ocr-batch-user"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-eu/scans/incoming/* for reading the originals. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-eu/scans/text/* for the extracted output. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket itself, with an s3:prefix condition limited to scans/incoming/, so the workers can enumerate pending files. The user's access keys should be rotated on a fixed schedule, since the policy trusts that user identity directly. Verify the setup by placing a two-page PDF in scans/incoming/ and checking for a matching text file in scans/text/.

This guide covers the bucket policy for an OCR pipeline that reads scanned PDF files from the scans/incoming/ prefix of the bucket records-archive-eu and writes searchable text layers to the scans/text/ prefix. The extraction is performed by the GlyphScan service on behalf of account 444455556666. Create a statement with Effect set to Allow and Principal set to {"Service": "glyphscan.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-eu/scans/incoming/* for reading the originals. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-archive-eu/scans/text/* for the extracted output. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket itself, with an s3:prefix condition limited to scans/incoming/, so the service can enumerate pending files. Restrict the statement with aws:SourceAccount set to 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:glyphscan:eu-west-1:444455556666:pipeline/*, since the service principal is shared by all customers. Verify the setup by placing a two-page PDF in scans/incoming/ and checking for a matching text file in scans/text/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for an image thumbnail generator that reads original photos from the originals/ prefix of the bucket catalog-images-prod and writes resized JPEG files to the thumbs/ prefix. The resizing function executes under the IAM role ThumbResizerRole in account 777788889999. Add a statement with Effect Allow and Principal {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/ThumbResizerRole"}. Permit s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images-prod/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images-prod/thumbs/*. Use a Deny statement with a NotResource element if you need to prevent the role from writing outside thumbs/. Because the role is the trusted identity, any workload that can assume it inherits this access, so limit the role's trust policy accordingly. Set the Content-Type metadata on uploaded thumbnails to image/jpeg in the resizer configuration. To test, upload a 4000x3000 pixel image to originals/ and confirm that a 320-pixel-wide thumbnail appears in thumbs/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for an image thumbnail generator that reads original photos from the originals/ prefix of the bucket catalog-images-prod and writes resized JPEG files to the thumbs/ prefix. The resizing is performed by the PixelTrim service in account 777788889999. Add a statement with Effect Allow and Principal {"Service": "pixeltrim.amazonaws.com"}. Permit s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images-prod/originals/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images-prod/thumbs/*. Use a Deny statement with a NotResource element if you need to prevent the service from writing outside thumbs/. Because the service principal is not tied to one customer, add aws:SourceAccount equal to 777788889999 and aws:SourceArn equal to arn:aws:pixeltrim:us-east-1:777788889999:resizer/catalog-thumbs. Set the Content-Type metadata on uploaded thumbnails to image/jpeg in the resizer configuration. To test, upload a 4000x3000 pixel image to originals/ and confirm that a 320-pixel-wide thumbnail appears in thumbs/.

This guide explains how to authorize an audio transcription workflow that reads recordings from the calls/audio/ prefix of the bucket support-voice-data and writes JSON transcripts to the calls/transcripts/ prefix. The workflow runs under an IAM role named TranscribeWorkerRole in account 202020303030. Define a statement with Principal {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::202020303030:role/TranscribeWorkerRole"} and Effect Allow. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::support-voice-data/calls/audio/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::support-voice-data/calls/transcripts/*. If the bucket uses SSE-KMS, the role also needs kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the key, granted in the key policy. Keep the audio prefix read-only by omitting any write action on it. Recordings are typically WAV or FLAC files up to 2 GB, so confirm that the role's session duration covers the longest expected job. Validate the configuration by running one recording through the workflow and opening the resulting transcript file for timestamps and speaker labels.

This guide explains how to authorize an audio transcription workflow that reads recordings from the calls/audio/ prefix of the bucket support-voice-data and writes JSON transcripts to the calls/transcripts/ prefix. The workflow is run by the VoiceLedger service in account 202020303030. Define a statement with Principal {"Service": "voiceledger.amazonaws.com"} and Effect Allow. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::support-voice-data/calls/audio/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::support-voice-data/calls/transcripts/*. If the bucket uses SSE-KMS, the service also needs kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the key, granted in the key policy. Keep the audio prefix read-only by omitting any write action on it. Recordings are typically WAV or FLAC files up to 2 GB, so add a condition with aws:SourceAccount equal to 202020303030 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:voiceledger:*:202020303030:transcription-job/* to scope the grant to your own jobs. Validate the configuration by running one recording through the workflow and opening the resulting transcript file for timestamps and speaker labels.

This guide shows how to grant access for a document conversion service that reads DOCX files from the bucket contracts-drafts under the word/ prefix and writes PDF output to the pdf/ prefix. The conversion workers use an IAM role named DocConvertRole in account 515151626262. Create a statement with Principal {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::515151626262:role/DocConvertRole"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/word/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/pdf/*. Add s3:GetObjectVersion for the word/ prefix if versioning is enabled and conversions must reference a specific revision. Output files should be written with the bucket-owner-full-control ACL, which you can enforce using a condition on s3:x-amz-acl. Source documents are limited to 100 MB each in this deployment. Test the policy by uploading a sample DOCX and confirming that a PDF with the same base name is created within the pdf/ prefix.

This guide shows how to grant access for a document conversion service that reads DOCX files from the bucket contracts-drafts under the word/ prefix and writes PDF output to the pdf/ prefix. The conversion is performed by the PageShift service in account 515151626262. Create a statement with Principal {"Service": "pageshift.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/word/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/pdf/*. Add s3:GetObjectVersion for the word/ prefix if versioning is enabled and conversions must reference a specific revision. Output files should be written with the bucket-owner-full-control ACL, which you can enforce using a condition on s3:x-amz-acl, and you should add aws:SourceAccount equal to 515151626262 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:pageshift:*:515151626262:converter/*. Source documents are limited to 100 MB each in this deployment. Test the policy by uploading a sample DOCX and confirming that a PDF with the same base name is created within the pdf/ prefix.

This guide configures the bucket policy for an invoice data extraction pipeline that reads scanned invoices from the invoices/raw/ prefix of the bucket finance-intake-prod and writes structured CSV results to the invoices/parsed/ prefix. The extraction job runs under the IAM role InvoiceParserRole in account 818181929292. Add a statement that names {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::818181929292:role/InvoiceParserRole"} as the Principal. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-intake-prod/invoices/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-intake-prod/invoices/parsed/*. Add an explicit Deny on s3:PutObject for invoices/raw/* so that originals cannot be overwritten. Enable S3 Object Lock in governance mode on the raw prefix if retention rules apply. The role's permissions boundary should be reviewed, because it can silently narrow the effective access. Confirm the result by processing one invoice image and checking that the CSV in invoices/parsed/ lists the vendor, date, and total fields.

This guide configures the bucket policy for an invoice data extraction pipeline that reads scanned invoices from the invoices/raw/ prefix of the bucket finance-intake-prod and writes structured CSV results to the invoices/parsed/ prefix. The extraction job is run by the LedgerRead service in account 818181929292. Add a statement that names {"Service": "ledgerread.amazonaws.com"} as the Principal. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-intake-prod/invoices/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::finance-intake-prod/invoices/parsed/*. Add an explicit Deny on s3:PutObject for invoices/raw/* so that originals cannot be overwritten. Enable S3 Object Lock in governance mode on the raw prefix if retention rules apply. Constrain the service statement with aws:SourceAccount equal to 818181929292 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:ledgerread:*:818181929292:extraction/*. Confirm the result by processing one invoice image and checking that the CSV in invoices/parsed/ lists the vendor, date, and total fields.

This guide covers the bucket policy for a loudness normalization job for podcast audio that reads raw episodes from the episodes/raw/ prefix of the bucket podcast-production and writes normalized MP3 files to the episodes/final/ prefix. The job executes under the IAM role LoudnessRole in account 303030404040. Create a statement with Principal {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::303030404040:role/LoudnessRole"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-production/episodes/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-production/episodes/final/*. Target loudness is -16 LUFS, which is configured in the job definition and not in the policy. Cross-account access is not needed here, so the policy should not name any other account ID. Retain raw episodes for 30 days using a lifecycle rule on the raw prefix. Run a single episode through the job and check that the file in episodes/final/ reports the target loudness when analyzed.

This guide covers the bucket policy for a loudness normalization job for podcast audio that reads raw episodes from the episodes/raw/ prefix of the bucket podcast-production and writes normalized MP3 files to the episodes/final/ prefix. The job is executed by the LevelMatch service in account 303030404040. Create a statement with Principal {"Service": "levelmatch.amazonaws.com"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-production/episodes/raw/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-production/episodes/final/*. Target loudness is -16 LUFS, which is configured in the job definition and not in the policy. Access should be limited to your own account, so set aws:SourceAccount to 303030404040 and aws:SourceArn to arn:aws:levelmatch:*:303030404040:job/*. Retain raw episodes for 30 days using a lifecycle rule on the raw prefix. Run a single episode through the job and check that the file in episodes/final/ reports the target loudness when analyzed.

This guide describes the bucket policy for a deep-zoom image tiling workflow that reads large TIFF scans from the bucket archive-maps-prod under the tiff/ prefix and writes tile pyramids to the tiles/ prefix. The tiling workers run under an IAM user named tiler-service-user in account 909090101010. Add a statement with Effect Allow and Principal {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::909090101010:user/tiler-service-user"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::archive-maps-prod/tiff/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::archive-maps-prod/tiles/*. Because each source image can produce thousands of small tile objects, include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on tiles/* for cleanup of failed uploads. Source TIFF files can exceed 5 GB, so the client should use multipart uploads and ranged reads. Rotate the user's access keys every 90 days, as this identity holds long-term credentials. Test by tiling one scan and verifying that the tiles/ prefix contains zoom-level folders from 0 up to the maximum level.

This guide describes the bucket policy for a deep-zoom image tiling workflow that reads large TIFF scans from the bucket archive-maps-prod under the tiff/ prefix and writes tile pyramids to the tiles/ prefix. The tiling is performed by the MosaicCut service in account 909090101010. Add a statement with Effect Allow and Principal {"Service": "mosaiccut.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::archive-maps-prod/tiff/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::archive-maps-prod/tiles/*. Because each source image can produce thousands of small tile objects, include s3:AbortMultipartUpload on tiles/* for cleanup of failed uploads. Source TIFF files can exceed 5 GB, so the service uses multipart uploads and ranged reads. Add aws:SourceAccount equal to 909090101010 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:mosaiccut:*:909090101010:tiling-job/* so that other customers of the service cannot reach this bucket. Test by tiling one scan and verifying that the tiles/ prefix contains zoom-level folders from 0 up to the maximum level.
